summary: Round 6, prose only: no production logic, no wire change, no object-store request added, moved or authorised by this diff. I ATTACKED THE NARROWED JUSTIFICATION FIRST, AS ASKED, AND IT HOLDS ON THE BYTES. SegmentWriter.java:98 sets `byteStart = SegmentFormat.PREAMBLE_BYTES + headerLen` and advances it per block, so the event's byteStart is an ABSOLUTE offset within the object, not a data-section-relative one -- no header read is needed to convert it. SegmentKey.headerLenOf plus SegmentFormat.PREAMBLE_BYTES name the header range, both public and in `format`, which `client` depends on. The grant is key-scoped with no range (Decision (c)), so one presigned URL serves both requests. A consumer therefore holds, at event-receipt time and with nothing else, everything needed to issue GET [byteStart, byteStart+byteLen) and GET [0, PREAMBLE+headerLen) at the same instant; without the event's copies the slice bounds come only from RunEntry via the directory, so the two requests are strictly ordered. One round trip is real, it is exactly one, and 'parallelism, not possibility' is the correct statement of it. The price re-derives cleanly and independently (7/129 = 5.43%, 11,200/206,400 = 5.43%, 11,200/8,388,608 = 0.1335%, 206,400/8,388,608 = 2.4605%, cross-check 0.1335/2.4605 = 5.43%, 40.4x; measured 6/128 = 4.69%), and the presence byte really is unconditional in v3 (SubscriptionEvent.java:482-492), so 'removal saves the varints AND the flag' is true. Round-5's two majors are fixed at their named sites: ADR-0043's Status block no longer says 'because no range is expressible' and now blames the 'without a directory read' half, and ADR-0044's Decision (b) at :114-118 carries the RTT argument with the weakness stated. WHAT BLOCKS IS THE SWEEP, NOT THE ARGUMENT: the refuted sentence -- the fields are 'the only thing making a bounded read possible' -- is still ASSERTED, as a live reason, in two places this commit wrote. ADR-0044's own Consequences at :292 says '(b) keeps the bounded read possible at a cost of 5.4%', 175 lines below the paragraph that says they buy parallelism and not possibility; and the M5.66 row this commit ADDS to backlog.md:126 opens by saying the fields were kept 'on the ground that they are the only thing making a bounded read possible later'. Neither site is in the sweep table, which the record calls THE SINGLE ENUMERATION and which M5.66's criterion 3 points at instead of copying -- so neither would ever be swept. This is the one-of-two-places defect the record has now spent six rounds on, reproduced inside the fix for round 5's instance of it, and it lands in the two texts that decide the field's fate: the record's bottom-line summary and the owning row's first sentence.

findings.title: ADR-0044's Consequences still asserts the refuted claim as the bottom line: '(b) keeps the bounded read possible at a cost of 5.4%'
findings.summary: :290-293 reads 'What this forecloses: nothing, deliberately. Both (a) and (b) are decisions to *not* spend a reversal. (a) keeps all three adapter options open at the cost of one milestone's delay; (b) keeps the bounded read possible at a cost of **5.4% of the subscription stream** (0.134% of the segment).' The parallel construction makes the claim explicit: what the 5.4% BUYS is the bounded read's possibility. Decision (b) at :114-118, written in this same commit, says the opposite in as many words -- 'the fields buy **parallelism, not possibility**' -- and :102-112 gives the reason (RunEntry carries the same extent in the directory, SegmentReader.find resolves it, the two-request design fetches that directory first for codecFlags). (b1) at :239-248 repeats the correct version a third time: 'Decision (b) above no longer claims the fields make a bounded read POSSIBLE ... only that they save one round trip.' So the record retires the claim at :105, at :117 and at :241, and then restates it as the summary of what was bought at :292. It is also false on the record's own (b3): the bounded read needs ONE new SegmentReader entry point and no format change, so removing the fields would not foreclose it at all -- it would cost one RTT and a re-add. The sweep table at :318-339 has no row for this file's own Consequences section, so criterion 3's artifact does not cover it.
findings.failure_scenario: 'What this forecloses' is the section a reader opens to learn what the decision bought without re-reading the argument -- it is the summary line a milestone review and a later re-pricer quote. M5.66's owner is obliged by criterion 3 to revisit this record; they read Decision (b) (one RTT), then read at the end that (b) 'keeps the bounded read possible'. If their measurement says one RTT is not worth 5.4%, the removal arm now reads as foreclosing the bounded read entirely -- the arm ADR-0044 explicitly says would SUPERSEDE it -- so they decline removal on a reason this record killed 175 lines earlier, and the fields are argued a fifth time. That is precisely the 'justification that outlived the thing justifying it' defect (b2) at :261-265 is rejected for, in the file rejecting it.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the (b) clause of :292 to the surviving claim: '(b) keeps the bounded read ONE ROUND TRIP CHEAPER -- not possible; the directory already carries the extents -- at a cost of 5.4% of the subscription stream (0.134% of the segment).' Then add a sweep-table row for this file's own Consequences and Alternatives sections, since the round-5 fix touched Decision (b) and (b1) and reached neither.

findings.title: The M5.66 row added by this commit opens with the refuted justification, in the cell whose owner decides whether the fields stay
findings.summary: The new row reads: 'ADR-0044 KEPT SubscriptionEvent's byteStart/byteLen WITH NO READER CONSUMING THEM, priced at 5.4% of the subscription stream they travel on ... on the ground that they are the only thing making a bounded read possible later'. That is the exact sentence ADR-0044:102-105 quotes and retires ('An earlier draft of this record kept them as "the only thing that makes a bounded read possible later". They are not.') and that M5.45f's own State cell at backlog.md:67 records as refuted by round 5. The same row compounds it further on: 'which makes this row cheaper than its first framing and the coordinates more clearly worth their 5.4%' -- M5.66 being cheap does not make the coordinates worth more, because their benefit is one RTT at any price of M5.66. The sweep table names its patterns as byteStart, byteLen, coordinates, byte range, M5.44, ADR-0043, VERSION_3 and enumerates sites; backlog.md matches four of those patterns and appears in no row, so the file the project calls authoritative is outside the enumeration M5.66's criterion 3 is told to treat as THE list.
findings.failure_scenario: backlog.md is authoritative and `next-task` sends an agent to the row before anything else; M5.66's owner reads their own cell first and the ADR second. Their cell's first sentence tells them the fields are kept because they are the ONLY thing making a bounded read possible -- which makes criterion 2's second arm, 'OR THE COORDINATES COME OFF THE WIRE', self-defeating by construction: removing them would remove the possibility. So the owner measures the crossover, finds one RTT is not worth 5.4%, and declines removal anyway, or never frames removal as live. Either way the question ADR-0044 created this row to own is decided on the reason ADR-0044 exists to retire, which is the fourth reopening in the sequence (0042 removed, 0043 restored, 0043 reopened, 0044 closed). And because backlog.md is in no sweep row, criterion 3's 'every site in the table is corrected or re-confirmed' will pass with this site never looked at.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the M5.66 cell's opening ground to the surviving one: '... on the ground that they save ONE ROUND TRIP on a bounded read -- NOT that they make one possible, which RunEntry's directory copy already does -- and that one RTT against 5.4% is the number this row must take.' Drop or re-base the 'more clearly worth their 5.4%' clause. Add a sweep-table row for backlog.md's M5.45f and M5.66 cells so the authoritative file is inside the enumeration.

findings.title: The surviving justification is 'act on the wire copy before the authoritative one arrives', and nothing says which copy wins when they disagree
findings.summary: Decision (b) now keeps the fields for exactly one property: the slice GET is issued WITHOUT waiting for the header. That property is only available by acting on the event's copy of an extent for which the segment's own directory is authoritative -- the record establishes at :106-112 that RunEntry carries the same numbers and that the reader fetches the directory anyway, milliseconds later. The record does not name that as a cost of what it is keeping, and M5.66's criteria (backlog.md:126) require 'a consumer that uses the EVENT's coordinates to drive it' without requiring the two copies be checked to agree. Round 5's suggested fix asked for exactly this clause and the narrowing answered the other half of the finding only.
findings.failure_scenario: M5.66's reader issues the slice from the event's byteStart concurrently with the header GET. The directory arrives and disagrees -- a replayed v3 event against a rewritten object, a publisher off-by-one, a truncated frame that passed the decoder's bounds guards. With no stated rule, the natural implementation decodes the slice it already has: a run decoded from the wrong offset, which either throws inside the record loop or yields records from the neighbouring run, with the offset advancing. The cross-check costs nothing (the directory is in hand before decode) but has to be asked for; it is the sequential design that is safe by construction, and the parallel one this field exists to enable that is not.
findings.suggested_fix: One sentence in Decision (b), after 'parallelism, not possibility': the parallel issue means acting on a DUPLICATE of a fact the directory owns, so a bounded reader compares the event's extent with the RunEntry it fetched and refuses on disagreement rather than decoding the slice it already holds. Then M5.66's criterion 2 can assert it.
